title: closure: move the round-9 roster/state docs into main, and record the R9-ROW-STALE class (#2086)
body:
This is step 1 of the round-9 closure's ref prune (group R9-CLOSURE-BRANCHES, #2086): move the roster and the state docs into main, so their refs stop being live infrastructure and can be archived as tags and deleted. It is the prerequisite for the prune; this pull request touches no production code. It also folds in the `R9-ROW-STALE` class the closure-records pull request's RCA file names.

## Head

205a45208e7d3a44eca0b2d5e15a8ef02c2c0a9b

## Summary

Two refs are read at run time and so cannot be deleted while a reader exists:

- `handoff/audit-r9-fixplan` is the roster read by `.github/workflows/tests.yml` as `ROSTER_REF` for the record beat;
- `handoff/audit-r9-plan` carries the three generated state docs.

This pull request moves both into main and retargets the reader:

- **the roster** lands at `dev/programme/rosters/wave-r9-groups.json`, a byte copy of the ref's `wave-r9-groups.json` (same blob, `2ffe98c6`). That directory is deliberate: `tests/layout.json` already reserves `dev/programme/rosters/*.json` for rosters, and the file must NOT sit under `.claude/workflows/`, where the basename `wave-*-groups.json` is scanned as a LIVE web-fix-wave roster by `brief_lint.mjs` (the `briefs` job, which refuses a carry that collides with a live group) and by `check-wave-script.mjs` (the `wave-script` job, which asserts every committed roster's stages are web-fix-wave's vocabulary). The round-9 roster uses the round-9 orchestrator's vocabulary (`handoff`, `fixing`, `deferred`, `not-started`, `rca-done`, `refuted`) and carries none of web-fix-wave's pointer keys, so committing it under `.claude/workflows/` would redden BOTH jobs on main; `.claude/workflows/wave-*-groups.json` stays reserved for a live roster.
- **the state docs** land at `dev/programme/round9/state/{PLAN-TABLE,RESUME-CURRENT,NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT}.md`, a copy of the ref's `handoff/round9/state/`; `tests/layout.json` gains a `dev/programme/round9/**` glob so the new directory is categorised, and `dev/programme/rosters/` and `dev/programme/round9/` join its `historical` list -- the roster's briefs and the state docs are historical text whose citations keep the paths that were true when they were written (`tools/audit/app_push.sh`, `tools/audit/briefs/fixer.md`, `tools/audit/round9/` and 41 more), which the layout guard's `new-reference` check otherwise refuses in a new file (331 refusals before the `historical` entry).
- **`roster_lib.ROSTER_PATH`** now names the new roster, with the pre-closure path as a fallback, so a caller still pointed at the old ref reads the roster through the transition rather than the neutral phrasing. `roster_edit.py`'s copy of the constant is kept in step, and `state_docs.py`'s `--roster-ref` default moves to `origin/main`.
- **`ROSTER_REF`** in `.github/workflows/tests.yml` defaults to `main` (the repo variable `RECORD_ROSTER_REF` is unset, so this default is the whole of it).

Step 2 (the citation sweep) is settled here too: `git grep` finds 58 files naming the roster, state and audit-evidence refs, and NOT ONE is a linter input -- the only roster on main (`wave-3l-groups.json`) names none, and the two live carries (`carry-1774`, `carry-1795`) name `handoff/audit-r9-fixplan` only inside their `_comment` field, which `brief_lint` does not lint. Every citation is prose in a historical record (`dev/audit/**`, `dev/archive/**`), a docstring, or provenance data; each is dispositioned **keep**, because the refs are archived as tags at the same sha (`archive/handoff/<name>`) and so remain resolvable by tag rather than by branch. The proof is the `briefs` job, which is green with zero citations to retarget.

**Folded in (the same closure-record family): the `R9-ROW-STALE` class the closure-records RCA file names.** The file `dev/audit/rca/R9-RCA-ROW-STALE.md` (landed by the open closure-records pull request #2193) ends "Class citation. Add an `R9-ROW-STALE` class to `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`"; this carries it. Because the class id must appear in THREE places that `check-wave-script.mjs` and `agreement.mjs` hold equal, one entry is three files: the class in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` (three round-9 instances `#2111`, `#2150/#2151`, `#2176/#2182`; barrier = `record_row.py`'s `modified_lines`/`_rewrite_refusal` pair plus `delivery_status.py`'s `open_anchored` reporter arm; a class-level `_rca` index entry; process state (c)), the enum in `dev/audit/config/finding.schema.json`, and `CLASS_GUESS` in `.claude/workflows/audit-find.js`. Two divergences from the request, both forced by the schema and named here rather than taken silently: the ledger has no `closed` class status (its values are `barriered`/`open`/`detector`/`prototype-only`, and `fold_ledger.py` derives the `barriered_any` trigger from `barriered`), so the status is **`barriered`**; and the `_rca` entry's `in_tree_home` is `null` -- the document is on #2193's branch, not on this one, and a non-null home DANGLINGs until it merges. `nearest_existing` is `I3` (as the sibling process-class `N-postreview-merge-red` uses) with the mechanism difference stated in the entry.

## Figures

- `node tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs` -> TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 47 file(s)
- `node tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs` -> 170 passed, 0 failed
- `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs` -> TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 40 policy file(s)
- `python3 tests/structure.py` -> STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED
- `python3 tools/audit/fold_ledger.py check` -> 0 violation(s)
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/state_docs.py --self-test` -> all checks passed
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py --self-test` -> 37 checks, 0 failed
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/plan_table.py --self-test` -> 25 checks, 0 failed
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/record_row.py --self-test` -> all checks passed

## Mutation proof

`roster_lib.show_roster` is driven at both paths: reading `HEAD` (the new roster path) and reading `origin/handoff/audit-r9-fixplan` (the legacy path, through the fallback) each return the same 170 groups. Removing the fallback makes the legacy read raise, which is the pre-closure caller's break. The ledger half: dropping the `R9-ROW-STALE` entry from `finding.schema.json`'s enum reddens `check-wave-script`'s `class_guess is exactly the ledger ids plus "new"`; adding it to the ledger without the enum (or the `CLASS_GUESS` regex) reddens the same check and `agreement.mjs`'s `finding-class-id` pair.

## Null control

With the roster at `dev/programme/rosters/` and nothing under `.claude/workflows/` matching `wave-*-groups.json`, `brief_lint.mjs` and `check-wave-script.mjs` report the SAME verdicts as before the file was added (0 errors; 170 passed, 0 failed). The negative control for the alternative: the same bytes committed under the live path `.claude/workflows/wave-r9-groups.json` make `brief_lint` error on `carry-1795` (a carry colliding with the live group R9-UX-6) and `check-wave-script` fail on the stage vocabulary and 312 missing pointer keys -- and the layout guard refuses the file, since `.claude/workflows/*.json` is in no category.

## Red checks

none: no check went red on this branch.

## Architecture score

n/a: no production code changed (`custom_components/` untouched); no `arch-score` rise to explain.

## Forward-carry

`dev/governance/roles/fixer.md` -- the state-docs BEAT (`state_docs.py beat`) writes to the orphan ref `handoff/audit-r9-plan`; once this pull request's state-docs snapshot is on main the beat is retired, and step 3/4 of #2086 archives that ref as a tag and deletes the branch. `dev/programme/HANDOVER.md` should record the retirement. The `R9-ROW-STALE` `_rca` entry's `in_tree_home` is `null` because its document lands with #2193, not here; a one-line follow-up sets it to the path once #2193 merges, and `fold_ledger.py check` is the detector for that.

## Friction

`brief-citations.md`: contradiction: the R9-CLOSURE-BRANCHES group brief's step 1 says move the roster "into main", but main's live-roster scans read `.claude/workflows/wave-*-groups.json` as a web-fix-wave roster, so the literal path reddens `briefs` and `wave-script`; resolved by the roster directory `tests/layout.json` already reserves.
